data.name: Melech
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, the name Melech is derived from the word melekh, which means 'king' or 'monarch'. In biblical times, Melech was a common name for kings and rulers, including King Solomon and King Hezekiah.

in_hebrew.name: מֶלֶך
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם-המלך, מעצב-המצפן, שלט-האדם, חכם-אדם, רח-אדם, דב-אדם, הגד-אדם, עצל-אדם, אדם-הגד-אדם. שמו של מלך-ישראל, הכובש-עיר, הבונה-מזבח. נביא-ישראל, חכם-האל, שליח-אדם.

in_greek.name: Μέλεχ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Μέλεχ είναι ο τίτλος των βασιλέων του Ισραήλ. Ο Μέλεχ είναι και ο τίτλος των σοφών και των φίλων του Θεού. Μετά το θάνατο του Μωυσή, ο Μωυσή διέταξε τους Λευίτες να εκλέξουν ένα άντρα από τα κλάδους του Ααρών και των Ελεάζαρ, και να τον κάνουν να δώσει το όνομά του στον άντρα, τον οποίο θα επέλεγαν, ο οποίος θα ήταν ο αρχιερέας. Ο Μέλεχ ήταν ο τίτλος του αρχιερέα, ο οποίος θα είχε την εξουσία να δίνει το όνομά του στην πόλη, και να την αφιερώνει στο Θεό.

in_latin.name: Melech
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen regis Israel, rex pacis, rex sapientiae. Etiam nomen viri sapientis, viri amici Dei. Post mortem Moysis, Moyses iussit Levitas ut eligant virum de tribubus Aaron et Eleazar, et ut nomen eius imponerent viri, quem eligissent, qui erat sacerdos. Melech erat nomen sacerdotis, qui habebat potestatem nomen civitatis imponere, et civitatem Deo dicare.

in_english.name: Melech
in_english.long_meaning: The name Melech originates from the Hebrew root MLK, meaning 'king' or 'conqueror'. In biblical times, Melech was the title of the kings of Israel. Melech is also associated with wisdom, as seen in the book of Proverbs, where Melech is mentioned alongside other wise men. The name Melech is also linked to the character of Melech, a wise and just king who ruled over Israel during the period of the judges.

biblical_reference.note: Melech is mentioned in the context of the Israelites' struggles against the Philistines.

data.cultural_impact: The name Melech holds a significant cultural impact as it was the title of various kings and rulers in the Hebrew Bible. It symbolizes power, authority, and sovereignty. The usage of this name echoes the rich history and traditions of ancient Israel and its monarchy system.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Melech signifies godly leadership and ruling with righteousness. It reminds us of God as the ultimate King who rules over all creation and calls us to live in accordance with His judgments and decrees. The name Melech can also inspire us to strive for godliness and to rule our own lives with the same wisdom and authority that a king would possess.

historical_references.reference: King Melech I of Israel, son of King David, ruled from approximately 970 to 931 BCE. He is known for his efforts to centralize the monarchy and expand the kingdom's territories.

King Melech of Tyre, also known as Melkart or Melqart, was a Phoenician god worshiped in the city of Tyre around the 1st millennium BCE. The king's name may have been derived from the god's name, and the god was often depicted as a monarch.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Melech' originated from the Hebrew language and translates to 'king' in English. In modern usage, this name is often associated with royalty, power, and leadership. In the context of tabletop role-playing games, Melech may be the name of a powerful monarch ruling over a vast kingdom. In literature and poetry, Melech might be a character in a mythological or fantastical story, such as a king of the gods or a powerful sorcerer. In video games, Melech may be the name of a boss character or a powerful item that bestows leadership abilities.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Grace Melech in New York, United States credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Melech, which means "King, Monarch, Ruler". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Melech, meaning "king" in Hebrew, represents the inner ruler or sovereign in each of us, guiding us to govern our thoughts, emotions, and actions with wisdom, love, and righteousness, reflecting the divine kingship of God within.
